description: Shape of one entry in memory/ARCHITECTURAL_DECISIONS.md. A decision record captures a choice that constrains future work, the alternatives that were rejected, and what would reverse it. Its purpose is to stop a future session re-litigating a settled question, and equally to stop it applying a settled answer to a case it was never settled for.

properties.note: `DEC-001` upward. Separate namespace from the router's `D-nn` series so a durable decision is never confused with a phase-local one.
The decision as one assertion, not a topic.
ISO-8601. When the decision was made, not when it was written down.
The situation that forced a choice. Without this a decision looks arbitrary, and the next reader 'fixes' it.
Why this option over the others.
What proves it was correct: a measurement, a file, a command output, a recorded observation. A decision with no evidence is a preference, and is labelled as one.
Options considered and rejected, each with why. This is the field with the highest long-term value: it is what prevents the same experiment being run twice.
What the decision costs as well as buys. A decision record with no stated cost reads as costless and gets applied too broadly.
What the decision applies to, and explicitly what it does not. Scope creep in decisions is the failure mode this field exists to prevent.
CURRENT means verified against the current repository. HISTORICAL means it was true and has not been re-checked.
Later decision id that replaced this one. Required when status is SUPERSEDED.
The observable condition that would justify revisiting. A decision with no reversal condition becomes permanent by inertia.

invariants: Only verified decisions are recorded. An unverified belief is recorded with status UNKNOWN, not stated as a decision.
No decision is invented to fill a category. An empty file is better than a plausible-sounding fabrication.
Contradicting current source does not delete the record; it sets status to SUPERSEDED with `supersededBy`.
`alternatives` may not be empty — a decision with no rejected options was not a decision.
Detail is not duplicated here; heavy detail links to the phase document that owns it.
